## 6. Engine boundaries

What the engine can do today, checked 2026-10-16 after the redesign build. "UI may offer" means a
control can be built on it now.

| Feature                                        | Engine today                                                                                                                                                         | UI may offer     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Pin a tray                                     | `Lock.position`; pins the whole stack (`src/app/actions.ts`)                                                                                                         | Yes              |
| Turn 90°                                       | `Lock.turn` on the chosen tray (`turnTray`); a pinned stack's pins turn with it; `freeTurn` removes it                                                               | Yes              |
| Swap two trays                                 | `swapLocks` swaps whole stacks and pins both                                                                                                                         | Yes              |
| Lock a tray's size                             | `Lock.size`                                                                                                                                                          | Yes              |
| Pins that conflict                             | Reported in `lockConflicts` with a `kind`; plan and pins kept                                                                                                        | Yes              |
| Why a tray can't turn                          | `canTurn` dry run through `resolveLocks` (`src/app/dryRun.ts`)                                                                                                       | Yes              |
| Try another arrangement with progress and Stop | `store.refit()`: about 3× budget, warm start, kept only if better                                                                                                    | Yes              |
| Undo and redo of every edit                    | `src/app/history.ts`, 100 steps, plan joins its edit's step                                                                                                          | Yes              |
| Engraved tray names                            | Letter glyphs, unique short names (`naming.ts`), `engraveNames`; two opposite walls and the underside                                                                | Yes              |
| Finger dips beside trays                       | A U cut from a solid filler's top where it touches a tray (`addFingerDips`, geometry 0.9.4); derived, no setting                                                     | No: no setting   |
| Box headroom (whole/part), stored on side      | `Box.headroom`, `headroomCoverage`, `storedOnSide`                                                                                                                   | Yes              |
| Growth, access, storage                        | `growth`/`separators`/`dividers`, `access`, `storage`                                                                                                                | Yes              |
| Copies (items and groups)                      | Separate trays, one per copy, all alike (`alikeOf`); a copy splits only when one tray can't fit, and evenly                                                          | Yes              |
| Groups                                         | One tray per copy; member order = compartment order (`Group.memberIds`; rows2, columns keep it between members)                                                      | Yes              |
| Flat decks in one well                         | Removable dividers, a finger cut per deck, on the front wall (`CardsComponent.flatDecks` "dividers")                                                                 | Yes              |
| Extra room (a group's empty well)              | `Group.growth` exists in the schema; no spare well is drawn yet                                                                                                      | No: engine work  |
| Settings presets and "N changed"               | Choice tables in `src/model/settings.ts`                                                                                                                             | Yes              |
| Project files, other-tab conflict              | `src/share/`, `src/app/persistence.ts`                                                                                                                               | Yes              |
| Saved status                                   | `src/ui/SavedStatus.tsx`                                                                                                                                             | Yes              |
| 3D on phones                                   | Needs WebGL; falls back to a sentence and the top view                                                                                                               | Yes              |
| Which tray doesn't fit                         | `misfitOf` heuristic plus `overBedKeys`; not a true culprit report. The plan marks that tray and its rail row says "Doesn't fit"; no figure is shown                 | Yes, approximate |
| How much room the items need                   | `volumeBudget` (`src/layout/volume.ts`): each item's smallest tray option, outer volume, against the box under the headroom; a lower bound, not a verdict below 100% | Yes              |
| Move a tray to the other layer                 | Layers are derived from stacks; no layer lock                                                                                                                        | No: engine work  |
| Keep it next to                                | Grouping merges into one tray; no adjacency                                                                                                                          | No: engine work  |
| Fix suggestions with outcomes                  | No suggestion generator; no side runs                                                                                                                                | No: engine work  |
| "Unpin one" with outcomes                      | Unpin works; its outcome needs a trial run                                                                                                                           | Unpin only       |
| Live "Still fits" in Settings                  | No side-run API                                                                                                                                                      | No: engine work  |

Known limits worth stating where they matter:

- Parts with no face that has room for their name stay plain (too short for the walls' band, too
  small or too thin a floor for the underside); the packing guide says "Too small for its name"
  (the download dialog does not count them: "Say less late in the flow"). Upper trays of
  about 9 mm or less may lose their wall names since geometry 0.8.0 (owner ruling pending). A
  merged part carries its name on walls only, never the underside.
- The combined 3MF lays parts in a grid that can spill past one bed for large inserts. No warning
  yet.
- Stop during export doesn't end the build already running in the geometry worker.
- With the rim and groove, a tray alone in its stack does not lock to its riser (its wall has no
  room for a groove); a riser under a tray with another on it does. With the stepped base every
  riser locks (2026-10-23).

### Phase 3: where this is going

From the plan's Phase 3 outline (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-16-ux-redesign.md`). Each needs
its own plan before UI work starts.

1. **Trial runs.** A second layout worker with its own cancel token; budget-limited runs that never
   touch the stored plan. Everything below depends on it.
2. **Fix suggestions with outcomes.** Candidates (lay figures flat, other storage, thinner walls,
   unpin one, another layer), each checked by a trial run, "Checking…" while they run. Replaces the
   bare no-fit and pin-conflict pills and the `misfitOf` heuristic.
3. **Live "Still fits" in Settings.** Draft settings feed a debounced trial run; the footer shows
   the result and the size and filament change.
4. **Layer lock.** A `level` lock kind, schema PATCH, enforced in `resolveLocks` and the move set;
   then "To the other layer" in the tray bar with dry-run reasons.
5. **Keep it next to.** `nextTo` on components (in `inputsHash`), a score term, a notice when it
   can't be met; then the editor's chooser.

Ship 4 and 5 in one release so they share one schema bump. Until each lands, MUST NOT add its
control, even disabled.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A tray never grows on its own, and growth is the last step of planning (2026-10-23, owner: "trays grow to fill their slot by default", "the extra becomes solid floor and wall: wide, awkward blocks I see in slicers", "I prefer spacers over grown trays"). A tray is its walls plus its wells and is bigger only because a well is. Each item that has the row (cards, tiles, bulk; not minis, not custom items) has one choice, in its contents' terms: "Room for more cards" / "Room for more tiles" / "Room for more pieces", None (default) / Some / As much as fits (`Component.room`: absent, a number or `"max"`; Some is a count of cards or tiles, or a percent of pieces, `src/model/room.ts`). The layout is planned on natural sizes plus each item's Some room, which is part of its size, with no room for growth in the context (`createCtx(…, { growth: false })`), so every gap is a spacer and the score charges it. Once a layout is chosen, the same tree is evaluated again with growth on (`withGrowth` in `optimize.ts`): the room left goes first into the wells of the items set to As much as fits (held by retention along a stack), then, by the insert-wide choice, as the setting says. The insert-wide "Fill the space that's left" replaces "Fill small gaps with": Separate spacers (default), Bigger wells (`Settings.biggerWells`: the room goes to the wells of items set to As much as fits first, then to the other wells as far as each kind may take it, the old Auto caps; what is still left is a spacer), Thicker walls and One thick wall (unchanged). Groups: a member set to As much as fits takes only its group tray's own leftover room and never makes the tray bigger (`CompartmentReq.fill`, now also for decks and tiles, held by retention); the wells of a member that asked for room are the ones that take it. Copies stay alike (hard rule 9): the room each set of alike trays may be given is the least any of its places leaves, so every copy's well grows by the same (`alikeGrowth`, `fill.ts`). Schema 0.3.0 (migration `model/migrate-0.3.ts`): growth off → None, Auto → None, a set amount → Some (mm turned into whole cards or tiles by the thickness of one, a bin's mm into a percent: 2 % a mm of its largest axis), Max → As much as fits; minis and custom items lose their growth and a group's `growth` (sizing never read it) goes. Every saved plan goes stale once (`PLANNING_MODEL` in the inputs hash): it was planned on grown trays with a score that treated growth as free. The room a stack forces on a lower tray (it is at least the footprint of everything above it) goes into the wells that can safely take it (bins, loose pieces, pockets, custom wells: `CompartmentReq.forcedOk`, `withForcedWells` in `realize.ts`), never into solid wall; a deck or a stack of tiles keeps it as wall (a deck in a much wider well topples) and the `swollen` score term steers the search away from stacking under a bigger tray. A size lock keeps its size and the room is wall: it is the person's choice. The last step puts what is left where it belongs (`packedToWall`, `fill.ts`): at the end of the row against the box wall, or with the trays that grow, and a bottom tray moves off a wall its leaf touches so the room lies against it, unless a finger cut passes through that side. Reverses minimal-trays spec §1 ("a filler beside a tray is wasted space") and supersedes the rows on "Room for expansions", the Max line and Fill small gaps with. | Ruling (owner, 2026-10-23). Measured over every seed and fixture (this change's PR): growth off by default still fitted in 65 of 66 runs with about twice the spacers, and the owner prefers a spacer to a grown tray; with growth counted as free the optimizer chose layouts where trays filled their slot, and a tray that grew where its well could not (a deck's width, a bin's wall) made the extra solid floor and wall, even with spacers chosen. The three per-axis choices (width, length, height) asked people which side is which; one choice in the contents' terms lets the engine map it (a flat deck's room is a deeper well, an upright one's a longer well, bulk's is volume).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Growth by default (Auto); a growth choice per axis; growth counted free by the score; a tray that grows without a well that grows                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A split is even (2026-10-23, owner: "when a group/component with multiple entries is split, it also feels awkward when the split is 2:1:1 from 4 trays"): `offeredSplit` (`src/sizing/arrange.ts`) offers a split into k trays only when k divides the entries, by count and not by weight, up to four trays (`MAX_SPLITS` 4, `MAX_VARIANTS` 12): four entries go 2 + 2 or 1 + 1 + 1 + 1, three go one each. An item with no even split (five or seven entries) keeps the weighted two- and three-way splits | The packing guide says how to take each tray out (2026-10-23, from the investigation "lifting trays"): a Lift column in each layer's table with one line a row, and one "Taking it out." paragraph above the layers ("Start with the top layer. Read its table from the last row up, then do the same for the layer below."). There is no second list and no order number: the order out is the packing order read backwards, and `packingGuide` builds the packing order so that it holds (`takeOutOrder`): what stands on a tray is packed after it, and a solid block with nothing to hold is packed just before the neighbour it waits for (the one beside it with the best grip of its own, one in a layer above first). A part has a grip of its own by a finger cut (a tray's or a spacer's notch), a finger dip beside it, a scoop, an open pocket (a spare, riser or spacer printed with a pocket 5 mm deep or more), a finger dip cut across it or, for a divider, its top edge; the lines are "Lift it by the finger cut", "Lift it by the finger dip beside it", "Tip the pieces out, then lift it by the scoop", "Reach into its open pocket", "Lift it by the finger dip", "Empty one side first, then pinch its top edge", and for a tray with none of those "Empty it first, then lift it from inside". The first match wins, so a tray's own finger cut comes first, and the dip beside a tray (`dipsFacingTrays`) comes before its scoop. A filler's own dip is a grip only where it is cut across a thin strip (under 18 mm); a dip in one face of a thick filler is not, and such a block waits for a neighbour like any block with nothing to hold. A tray with only its contents to lift by, and a solid block, are flagged "No grip of its own" in their rows and named in one note above the layers; the block's line is "Take out <neighbour> first, then tip it out" ("Take out what <tray> holds first, then tip it out" for a spacer, "Tip it out of the box" with nothing beside it). A new way to lift a part is one entry in `GRIP_RULES` (`src/instructions/lift.ts`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Nothing on a tray's outside can be gripped: neighbours stand 0.2 mm away and the box wall 0.5 mm, so a whole tray comes out by a cut, a scoop or a pocket it has, or by what is in it, and a solid strip wedged between trays (Harbour Kings: 9.6 × 81 mm on Heroes beside Events, 10.6 × 152 mm on Dice beside Starter) only once a neighbour is out, unless a finger dip gives a hand a hold. A dip across a thin strip is a hold on the strip (finger and thumb pinch it at the slot) and on the trays it faces; a dip in one face of a thick filler is a hold on the tray it faces only: a U with vertical sides ends in the filler's own wall with nothing to pull on, and the filler's other face is against a tray or the box wall, so no thumb reaches it. A tray whose only way out is a dip beside it says so, and is not flagged. Seen before printing, "No grip of its own" is a thing to fix in the plan; found with the box full, it is a pry bar. One column because 0.11.0 merged the guide's two lists on purpose; reading the rows backwards is how a box is unpacked. A numbered column would number parts, which §2 (Names, not numbers) forbids. ## 8. Checklist for a UI change

- [ ] Every new string uses the Words table; `npx vitest run src/ui/copy.test.ts` passes.
- [ ] Trays are named, never numbered; measurements still show as mm, g and h.
- [ ] Every new control is at least 44 px, keyboard reachable, with a visible focus ring.
- [ ] A blocked control stays focusable and says why in one sentence.
- [ ] Toggles follow the `aria-pressed` rule and its Pin / Lock size exception; still one `h1`.
- [ ] Colours come from tokens or `shadeOf` / `shadeHex`; new tokens have a dark value; the same
      component looks the same in the list, plan, 3D and packing guide.
- [ ] Checked at 390, 820 and 1440 px, in light and dark, and with reduced motion.
- [ ] Nothing new is shown by default that could sit behind "More options" or "Exact numbers".
- [ ] No new Download entry point, banner, mode, link sharing, slicer claim, two-line pill or global
      key handler.
- [ ] The change is one undo step through `store.edit`; layout inputs are in `inputsHash`,
      print-only inputs are in the mesh cache key and not in the hash.
- [ ] The engine can back it today (section 6); otherwise it is marked as needing engine work and
      not shipped.
- [ ] Schema, geometry and app versions bumped per the README; a decision-log row added if a rule
      changed; `npm run build` passes.
